learningObjectives: Distinguish between Single-User and Multi-User workspaces and explain their access rules.
Navigate Tosca Commander and manage multiple sections using docking and tab groups.
Apply workspace best practices including the 4-Eye Principle, naming conventions, and folder structure.
Define a Subset and describe how it is exported and imported between workspaces.
Identify and navigate the System Under Test (SUT) using the Tricentis Automation Extension.

elements.description: A Model-Based Test Automation platform that enables codeless end-to-end testing by scanning the SUT to generate reusable test models.
The central IDE of Tricentis Tosca. Contains 9 sections in total; this course focuses on four core sections:
items: Modules — UI element models captured from the SUT
TestCases — ordered sequences of test steps
ExecutionLists — collections of TestCases to run
Requirements — business/technical requirements linked to tests

elements.description: The application being tested. In this course the SUT is the Tricentis Demo Web Shop at https://demowebshop.tricentis.com.

elements.text: Tosca Commander is like an aircraft cockpit: each instrument panel (section) gives you a different view of the same flight (project). You can rearrange panels to suit your workflow, but they all control the same aircraft.

bulletPoints: All Tosca work happens inside a Workspace — either local (Single-User) or shared (Multi-User).
Interface layout: Navigation pane (left, tree overview) + Working pane (middle, detailed editing area).
Sections can be rearranged: drag a tab to a docking destination OR right-click → 'New Vertical Tab Group'.
Save disables undo/redo — once you save in Tosca Commander, undo and redo are no longer available.

elements.description: Access is granted to whoever has the local workspace file. No administrator role is required — only local file access matters.
In a Multi-User workspace, objects must be checked out before editing. This locks them for other users until the editor checks them back in.
items: Check Out — marks the object as in-use; locked (read-only) for all other users
Check In — saves edits to the shared repository and releases the lock

elements.text: Single-User = a private notebook only you can read. Multi-User = a shared Google Doc that anyone on the team can edit simultaneously.

bulletPoints: Key exam rule: Single-User access = local file access only. No admin role needed, no user limit beyond one.

elements.description: A file containing Tosca artifacts (Modules, TestCases, etc.) that can be exported from one workspace and imported into another — the primary mechanism for sharing test assets between projects.

A subset provided by Tricentis containing pre-built Standard Modules, predefined virtual folders, and standard reports. Import it into any workspace to use ready-made assets immediately — no SUT scanning required for these modules.

bulletPoints: Subsets CAN be shared: exported from one workspace and imported into another.
The Tricentis Standard Subset gives you ready-made utility modules (keyboard, wait, file handling, etc.).

elements.description: A quality-control workflow ensuring a second reviewer validates all work before it is finalized.
items: In Work — tester is actively building/modifying the artifact
Ready for Approval — tester signals the work is complete and ready for review
Approved/Completed — reviewer confirms and closes the item

elements.description: Tricentis recommends three types of top-level Component folders in every repository:
items: Templates and references — reusable naming templates and sample structures shared across all projects
Relevant for all projects — shared Libraries and Standard Modules used by every project
Per-project folder — one per project, containing: Requirements, TestCaseDesign, TestCases, Execution, and Module sub-sections

elements.description: Apply consistent, descriptive names across all folders, modules, and test cases. Practical rule: choose the name first, then add a more granular description — not the other way around.

bulletPoints: 4-Eye state order: In Work → Ready for Approval → Approved/Completed (never skipped).
In Work and Ready for Approval each have one sub-folder per team member — Approved is shared.
Repository structure: 3 top-level Component folders — Templates+references, All-projects (Libraries/Modules), and one per project.
Per-project folder sub-sections: Requirements, TestCaseDesign, TestCases, Execution, Module.

examPitfalls.title: Single-User access ≠ administrator
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Exam scenarios describe a Single-User workspace and ask who can access it. Distractors include 'administrator only', 'up to 2 users with one being admin', or 'any user with network access'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Single-User access = the person who has the local workspace file. No administrator role, no user limit — only local file access matters.

examPitfalls.title: Subsets CAN be shared
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A distractor states 'A Subset is a file containing Tosca artifacts that cannot be shared with other projects'. This is the opposite of the truth.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Subsets ARE designed to be shared: exported from one workspace and imported into another. That is their entire purpose.

examPitfalls.title: Tosca Commander section navigation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how to view two sections side by side. 'Open Tosca Commander in a second window' is a common wrong answer.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Two correct methods: (1) Drag section tab to a docking destination. (2) Right-click tab → 'New Vertical Tab Group'.

examPitfalls.title: 4-Eye Principle order
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates mix up the status order — 'Approved → In Work → Ready for Approval' appears as a distractor.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Always: In Work → Ready for Approval → Approved/Completed. The tester sets 'Ready for Approval'; the reviewer sets 'Approved/Completed'.

examPitfalls.title: Tricentis Automation Extension specificity
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distractors mention 'any browser extension', 'Selenium WebDriver', or 'no extension needed'. The exam expects the Tricentis-specific extension name.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The required plugin is specifically called 'Tricentis Automation Extension for Chrome'.

examPitfalls.title: Save disables undo/redo
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question might describe a tester who saved their work and now wants to undo a recent change. Candidates may assume undo remains available.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Once you save in Tosca Commander, undo and redo are no longer available. Changes must be corrected manually after saving.

examPitfalls.title: Multi-User locking: check-out required to edit
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates may think any team member can freely edit objects in a Multi-User workspace. A distractor might say 'changes are merged automatically' or 'an admin can override the lock'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In Multi-User mode, objects must be checked out first. This locks them for all other users. Only a check-in by the holder releases the lock.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester works with a Tosca workspace stored on their local hard drive. A colleague wants to run tests from the same workspace simultaneously. Which workspace type is this, and can the colleague access it?

options.text: Multi-User Workspace — up to 2 users can work simultaneously.
Multi-User Workspace — the colleague can access it via the server.
Single-User Workspace — an administrator can grant the colleague access.
Single-User Workspace — only the user with the local file can access it; the colleague cannot.

practiceQuiz.hint: Local file = Single-User = only one person.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Single-User Workspace is stored locally and accessible only to the user who has that local file. No admin grant mechanism exists for Single-User — a Multi-User server-hosted workspace is needed for team collaboration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team lead wants to share Modules and TestCases from Project A with a colleague working in a completely separate workspace. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Export a Subset from Project A and import it into the colleague's workspace.
Copy the entire workspace folder and paste it into the colleague's directory.
Subsets cannot be shared between separate workspaces.
Use a Multi-User Workspace — artifacts are then available to everyone automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: Subsets are designed exactly for cross-project artifact sharing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Subset is a file containing Tosca artifacts that can be exported from one workspace and imported into another. This is the standard mechanism for sharing Modules and TestCases across separate projects.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs the Modules section and the TestCases section of Tosca Commander visible side by side. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Open Tosca Commander twice in two separate application windows.
Drag the section tab to a docking destination, or right-click the tab and select 'New Vertical Tab Group'.
Use the View menu to enable split-screen mode.
Sections cannot be displayed side by side in Tosca Commander.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two methods: drag-and-drop to docking, or right-click tab → New Vertical Tab Group.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tosca Commander allows side-by-side sections via two methods: (1) drag a section tab to a docking destination, or (2) right-click the tab → 'New Vertical Tab Group'. Opening a second instance is not the intended approach.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A module has been built by a tester and is ready for peer review. According to the 4-Eye Principle, which status should the tester assign before handing it to the reviewer?

options.text: Approved/Completed
In Work
Ready for Approval
Under Review

practiceQuiz.hint: The tester signals readiness; the reviewer approves.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 4-Eye Principle flow: In Work → Ready for Approval → Approved/Completed. The tester sets 'Ready for Approval' to signal the work is done; the reviewer then sets 'Approved/Completed'.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be installed in the browser before a tester can scan a web application with Tricentis Tosca?

options.text: No extension is needed; Tosca scans web applications natively.
A general-purpose web scraping extension such as Web Scraper.
The Selenium WebDriver plugin.
The Tricentis Automation Extension for Chrome.

practiceQuiz.hint: Tricentis provides its own named extension.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Tricentis Automation Extension for Chrome is required for Tosca to scan and interact with web applications. Generic extensions and Selenium are not used in Tosca's architecture.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE of the following are Tricentis-recommended workspace best practices?

options.text: Apply consistent naming conventions across modules, folders, and test cases.
Use Component folders: one for templates, one for all-projects content, and one per project.
Apply the 4-Eye Principle: In Work → Ready for Approval → Approved/Completed.
Store all modules at workspace root level to simplify access.

practiceQuiz.hint: Three are best practices; one is an anti-pattern.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Naming conventions (A), structured Component folders — templates, all-projects, and per-project (B), and the 4-Eye Principle (C) are all documented Tosca best practices. Storing modules at root without structure (D) is an anti-pattern. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the primary purpose of the Tricentis Standard Subset provided by Tricentis?

options.text: To provide a set of pre-built Standard Modules for common testing tasks.
To store the SUT's source code for offline testing.
To configure the connection to a Multi-User Workspace server.
To generate test execution reports automatically.

practiceQuiz.hint: It is a ready-made toolkit — no scanning needed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Tricentis Standard Subset contains pre-built Standard Modules for common execution tests. Import it into any workspace to immediately use these reusable modules without having to scan the SUT for standard operations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to Tricentis workspace best practices, components should be organized into three top-level folder types. Which combination correctly names all three?

options.text: Design | Development | Production
Templates and references | Relevant for all projects | Per-project folder
Modules | TestCases | ExecutionLists
Draft | In Review | Approved

practiceQuiz.hint: One holds templates, one is shared across all projects, one is scoped per project.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The three recommended Component folder types are: (1) Templates and references — reusable naming templates and sample structures; (2) Relevant for all projects — shared Libraries and Standard Modules used project-wide; (3) Per-project folder — one per project, containing Requirements, TestCaseDesign, TestCases, Execution, and Module sub-sections.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a Multi-User Tosca workspace, Tester A is currently editing a Module. Tester B tries to edit the same Module. What happens?

options.text: Tester B can override the lock using administrator rights.
Both testers can edit simultaneously — Tosca merges their changes automatically.
Tester B sees the Module as locked and must wait until Tester A checks it in.
The Module is only locked if Tester A has explicitly set it to Read-Only.

practiceQuiz.hint: Check-out = exclusive lock. Only one editor at a time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In a Multi-User workspace, editing requires checking out the object. The check-out places an exclusive lock visible to all other users. The lock is released only when Tester A checks the object back in. Simultaneous editing and force-override are not supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester makes several changes in Tosca Commander, then saves the workspace. A moment later, they realize the last change was a mistake. What can they do?

options.text: Use Ctrl+Z to undo the last change.
Close and reopen Tosca Commander to discard unsaved changes.
Use the 'Revert' option in the File menu to restore the pre-save state.
The change must be corrected manually — undo is no longer available after saving.

practiceQuiz.hint: Save = point of no return for undo.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tosca Commander disables undo and redo after a save operation. The tester must manually reverse any unwanted change. This is why it is important to review changes before saving.

quickRecap.value: Local file-based; only the user with the local file can access it. No server required.
Server-hosted; multiple users can access simultaneously. Objects must be checked out to edit (locks for others); checked in to release.
Portable file of Tosca artifacts. Exported from one workspace, imported into another.
Provided by Tricentis; contains pre-built Standard Modules for common test tasks.
In Work → Ready for Approval → Approved/Completed.
Side-by-side sections: drag tab to docking area OR right-click tab → 'New Vertical Tab Group'.
Naming conventions + 3 Component folders (Templates, All-projects, Per-project) + 4-Eye Principle.
Chrome browser plugin required for web application scanning and automation.
System Under Test — the application being automated. Course SUT: demowebshop.tricentis.com.
